# Hkdf&lt;D&gt;

Extract and expand in one call: the whole of HKDF.

```rux
pub func Hkdf<D: Digest>(prototype: D, salt: char8[..], material: char8[..], info: char8[..], into: var char8[..]) -> bool
```

Returns `false` for an output longer than 255 digests, exactly as [`HkdfExpand`](/docs/api/crypto/hkdf#hkdf-expand) does.

## Type parameters

| Name        | Description     |
| ----------- | --------------- |
| `D: Digest` | the digest type |

## Parameters

| Name        | Type            | Description                                          |
| ----------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `prototype` | `D`             | any value of the digest type, read only to select it |
| `salt`      | `char8[..]`     | the salt, which may be empty                         |
| `material`  | `char8[..]`     | the input keying material                            |
| `info`      | `char8[..]`     | the context and application-specific information     |
| `into`      | `var char8[..]` | receives the output                                  |

**Returns**: whether `into` was a length this construction can produce

<h3 id="hkdf-maximum-blocks"><code>HkdfMaximumBlocks</code></h3>

```rux
pub const HkdfMaximumBlocks: uint = 255;
```

The most blocks `Expand` can produce, since its counter is one byte.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Crypto/Src/Hkdf.rux#L17)

<h3 id="hkdf-extract"><code>HkdfExtract&lt;D&gt;</code></h3>

```rux
pub func HkdfExtract<D: Digest>(prototype: D, salt: char8[..], material: char8[..], into: var char8[..])
```

Extracts a pseudorandom key from `material`, salted with `salt`.
`into` must be exactly the digest's length. An empty salt is legal and means a string of that many zeros,
which is what the specification says — so an absent salt is not the same as no salt at all.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Crypto/Src/Hkdf.rux#L28)

<h3 id="hkdf-expand"><code>HkdfExpand&lt;D&gt;</code></h3>

```rux
pub func HkdfExpand<D: Digest>(prototype: D, key: char8[..], info: char8[..], into: var char8[..]) -> bool
```

Expands `key` into `into`, separated by `info`.
Returns `false` when `into` is longer than 255 digests, which is the most the one-byte counter can address;
nothing is written in that case. `info` names what the derived key is for, and two expansions of one key
under different info strings are unrelated.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Crypto/Src/Hkdf.rux#L57)

**Type parameters**

| Name        | Description     |
| ----------- | --------------- |
| `D: Digest` | the digest type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type            | Description                                          |
| ----------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `prototype` | `D`             | any value of the digest type, read only to select it |
| `key`       | `char8[..]`     | the key                                              |
| `info`      | `char8[..]`     | the context and application-specific information     |
| `into`      | `var char8[..]` | receives the output                                  |

**Returns**: whether `into` was a length this construction can produce
